# Experience & priorities transitions · 0.31.13

Two short screens explain the response changes within Get to know you. Each uses the existing compact introduction style, one small decorative icon, Back, and Keep going.

## Experience

**What have you tried?**

Next, tell us what you can do today. Think about school, home, hobbies, or helping someone.

Choose the statement that fits best—from “This is new to me” to “I could show someone else how.” Skills grow with practice.

## Priorities

**What matters most to you?**

Next, choose what you most want from work—like learning, helping people, or a steady future.

Pick up to three things that matter most to you. Tap a choice again to remove it.

## Navigation & saved work

- A transition appears when moving into each section, in both focused and all-question modes.
- Keep going records acknowledgment. Reloading or resuming does not repeat an acknowledged transition.
- Existing experience answers or priority selections resume without an inserted interruption.
- Back from the first question returns to its transition; Back from the transition restores the last required question in the preceding section.
- Question order, responses, scores, matching, saved notes, and completed steps stay intact.

## Verification

84 automated tests passed: 73 targeted profile, transition, experience, question-order, encouragement and refinement checks, plus 11 restart and student-rendering checks. Twelve tests specifically cover the new transitions, including focused and all-question modes, randomized order, persisted state, older drafts, and missing prerequisites.

An isolated fictional medicine student crossed both boundaries on a phone, continued into the new choices, reloaded, and went Back to verify saved selections. Both transition screens fit at 390 × 844 and 320 × 740 without horizontal overflow. Body copy is 18px, and both actions are visible. Real accounts and student data were not changed.

This is a presentation and navigation update, not a change to assessment content or scoring.
